extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in category theory, algebra, and topology
extracted.subtask_description: Conditions, definitions, and constructions needed to establish existence of adjoints (including the general and special adjoint functor theorems), together with related categorical notions (subobjects, generators, monads, T-algebras) and illustrative examples (CompHaus/Stone-Cech, Top, tensor products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of (Q,E)-algebra (algebra of type r)
rubrics_metrics.description: An algebra A of type r — a (Q,E)-algebra — is a set S together with an action A of Q on S which satisfies all the identities of E; S is the underlying set of the algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E is a set of ordered pairs (A,Φ) of derived operators of same arity; an action A of Q on S satisfies identity (A,Φ) iff A A = Φ A : s^n → s. Examples: take Q with product, inverse, identity element and E the group axioms to describe Grp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of (Q,E)-algebras preserve operators
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism g : A → A' of (Q,E)-algebras is a function g : S → S' on underlying sets which preserves all the operators of Q (and hence of A) in the sense that (formula) for all a_i ∈ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphisms must commute with every derived operator from Q; this characterization makes (Q,E)-Alg a category (a variety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution-set condition for existence of left adjoint (general AFT)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply the adjoint functor theorem one needs, for each object x of X, a small solution set of arrows i: x → G a (with a in A) such that every arrow x → G a' factors through some i in the set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The solution-set is the key finiteness/smallness hypothesis that replaces explicit constructions; examples show how to produce solution sets (free algebras generated by image of S, closures/dense subsets for compact Hausdorff spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: adjoint functor theorem produces free algebras for varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: For any variety of algebras the adjoint functor theorem yields a left adjoint for the forgetful functor (〈Q,E〉-Alg → Set); the solution set is obtained as in groups, producing free ring, free abelian group, free R-module, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: free fields do not exist because inverse to multiplication isn't everywhere defined; thus some algebraic 'types' are excluded because they are not algebraic systems in this sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: V: CompHaus → Set has left adjoint (Stone-Cech) via solution-set construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The forgetful functor V sending each compact Hausdorff space to its underlying set preserves (indeed creates) small products and equalizers; a small solution set of arrows s → V X is produced by considering closures/dense subsets and embeddings into the double power set of S, yielding the Stone-Čech compactification as the left adjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses Tychonoff for compactness, Hausdorff product topology, injection X ↪ 𝒫𝒫S via L_x = {U ⊆ S | x ∈ cl U}, and then taking all topologies on chosen sets to obtain a small solution set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of subobject (equivalence class of monics)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u: s → a and v: t → a are two monics with common codomain a, write u ≼ v when u factors through v; u == v when u ≼ v and v ≼ u; equivalence classes of these monics are the subobjects of a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often identify a monic u: s → a with its equivalence class; in familiar large categories (Grp, Rng, Ab, R-Mod) this corresponds to usual element-defined subobjects, but not always (e.g., Top).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullbacks of monics are monic (lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any pullback square, if f is monic then its pullback f' is monic (and dually for g and g').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is used to construct intersections (meets) of subobjects via pullbacks; proof uses uniqueness in pullback combined with monicity of f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of subobjects via pullback
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has pullbacks, the pullback of two monic subobjects u: s→a and v: t→a yields a monic w: p→a equivalent to the intersection (meet) of u and v; similarly, pullback of any J-indexed family (if it exists) gives their intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union (join) of subobjects requires additional hypotheses; intersections follow from existence of pullbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient objects as equivalence classes of epis
rubrics_metrics.description: Dually to subobjects, two epis r,s with domain a are equivalent when r = o s for some invertible o; the equivalence classes are quotient objects of a, ordered by r ≼ s when r factors through s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In categories where epis are onto (e.g., Grp), quotient objects correspond to factor groups; r ≼ s means 'more is divided out' in r than in s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generator (and cogenerator) criterion for a category
rubrics_metrics.description: A set S of objects generates C when for any parallel pair h ≠ h': c → d there exists s ∈ S and arrow i: s → c with h i ≠ h' i. Dually, Q cogenerates when for any parallel h ≠ h' : a → b there is q ∈ Q and g: b → q with g h ≠ g h'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-object generators include one-point set generating Set, ℤ generating Ab and Grp, R generating R-Mod; two-point set is a cogenerator in Set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'spanning' arrow for solution-set construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given G : A → X and arrow f: x → G a, f is said to span a when there is no proper monomorphism s → a in A such that f factors through G s → G a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The set of spanning arrows from x can serve as a solution set for x when appropriate pullbacks exist and are preserved by G (see lemma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: existence of spanning-factorization under pullback-preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: If in A every set of subobjects of an object a has a pullback, and G : A → X preserves all these pullbacks, then every arrow h: x → G a factors through an arrow f: x → G b which spans b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the pullback of all subobjects through which h factors; its universal property yields b and factorization f that spans b. This provides a canonical small solution set: all spanning arrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of spanning/arcs to produce solution set for varieties (free subalgebra bound)
rubrics_metrics.description: In varieties of algebras, given f: S → G A, the subalgebra A_f generated by f(S) has cardinality bounded by |S| and |Q|, so f factors through S → G A_f; the set of such arrows (for subalgebras generated by images of S) is a small solution set consisting of spanning arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hence the general AFT gives left adjoints (free algebras) without explicit presentation; this argument also shows why free fields fail to exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of tensor products via adjoint functor theorem (solution-set criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For modules A,B over commutative ring K, view Bilin(A,B; −) as a functor C ↦ Bilin(A,B;C). To get a solution set for given A,B, it suffices to consider bilinear maps that span C (i.e., do not factor through a proper submodule); then C is generated by finite sums f_i(a_i,b_i), so solution-set condition holds and the tensor product A ⊗ B exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bypasses explicit quotient constructions; relies on K-Mod being small-complete and Bilin being continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Initial-Object Theorem (conditions for initial object)
rubrics_metrics.description: If D is small-complete, has small hom-sets, a small cogenerating set Q, and every set of subobjects of each d ∈ D has an intersection, then D has an initial object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take product q0 = ∏_{q∈Q} q, intersect all subobjects of q0 to obtain r; show r is initial because at most one arrow r → d exists and for each d there is arrow r → d constructed from pullbacks of monics against a product of Q-arrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Adjoint Functor Theorem (SAFT) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be small-complete, have small hom-sets and a small cogenerating set Q, and suppose every set of subobjects of an object a ∈ A has a pullback; let X have small hom-sets. Then G : A → X has a left adjoint iff G preserves all small limits and all pullbacks of families of monics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity: any right adjoint preserves limits; sufficiency: construct initial objects in comma categories (x ↓ G) using Q' cogenerating (x ↓ G) and intersections/pullbacks of subobjects preserved/created by projection functor. Classical corollary: if A is well-powered (subobjects indexable by small sets) the requirement reduces to G continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: monics in comma category reflect monics in A
rubrics_metrics.description: An arrow h: (f:x→Ga,a) → (f':x→Ga',a') in (x ↓ G) is monic iff h: a → a' is monic in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projection (x ↓ G) → A creates all limits (hence kernel pairs); thus monicity in the comma category is equivalent to monicity in A—used in constructing intersections in (x ↓ G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary (classical SAFT / representability criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is small-complete, well-powered, with small hom-sets and a small cogenerating set, and X has small hom-sets, then G: A → X has a left adjoint iff it is continuous (preserves small limits). In particular any continuous K: A → Set is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-poweredness ensures that any set of subobjects has an intersection via usual pullbacks; this simplifies hypotheses of SAFT used often in classical sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of monad in a category
rubrics_metrics.description: A monad T = (T, η, μ) in a category X is an endofunctor T: X → X together with natural transformations η: Id → T (unit) and μ: T^2 → T (multiplication) making the associative and unit diagrams commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A monad is a monoid in the category of endofunctors (composition = product); diagrams correspond to associativity μ ∘ Tμ = μ ∘ μT and unit laws μ ∘ Tη = μ ∘ ηT = id.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction induces monad construction (T = G F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every adjunction (F,G,η,ε): X ⇄ A gives rise to a monad T = G F on X with unit η and multiplication μ = G ε F : G F G F → G F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking monad laws reduces to triangular identities of adjunction and interchange law for horizontal composition of natural transformations; example: free-group adjunction yields the free-group monad on Set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of T-algebra (Eilenberg–Moore)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a monad T = (T,η,μ) in X, a T-algebra (x,h) is an object x ∈ X with structure map h: T x → x making diagrams (h ∘ η_x = id_x) and (h ∘ μ_x = h ∘ T h) commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes the idea of an action of the 'monoid' T on x; category X^T of T-algebras fits into an adjunction X ⇄ X^T that recovers the monad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monad in a preorder is closure operation
rubrics_metrics.description: In a preorder P a monad T is a monotone function T: P → P with x ≤ T x and T(T x) ≤ T x; in a partial order these equalities yield T(T x) = T x, i.e., T is a closure operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides intuition: monads generalize closure operators; diagrams commute trivially because there is at most one arrow between any two objects in a preorder.
